_comment: How notes and the Sources list look when a story lands (tools/cite.py). Asked for by the author on the first pilot, 2026-10-03: "we need an introduction and references and citations". The writer's prose never carries apparatus; cite.py renders it from the claims, so the gates and a narration read the prose as written.
_notesStyle: appendix: clean chapters, one Notes appendix keyed by each paragraph's opening words, numbered Sources with links (the author's choice on the first pilot, 2026-10-03: per-sentence notes outweighed the text they supported). inline: a superscript after each run of sentences, notes per chapter.
notesIntro: Each note is keyed to the opening words of a paragraph. The numbers are the Sources that paragraph rests on.
sourcesIntro: Each note at the end of a chapter names the sources for the sentences before it.
numberedSourcesIntro: Numbered in the order the story first cites them.
_anchorMinScore: cite.py anchors writes an anchor only when the claim's own words point at one sentence this strongly (rare words weigh more) ...
_anchorMinMargin: ... and this far ahead of the next-best sentence. Everything else goes to the writer, because a note on the wrong sentence is worse than none.

titleBlock._comment: The book's title at the top of its first page (the introduction when there is one): the subject's name as a heading, then her or his years and the series. Apparatus, added when the story lands (cite.py book); the prose never carries it. Lawrence, 2026-10-04: "in the introduction there is no title in it so it takes a little bit to understand who we are talking about".
